model_player_facing_text: Cold rain spatters against the soot-dark stones that frame Cinderwatch's eastern gate, where frayed banners flutter in the damp breeze. The muddy approach is choked with refugees, wagons laboring through the mud, and foot traffic pressed tight beneath the watchful eyes of guards who hold the choke point firmly. A well-kept townhouse stands above the square, its noble colors a stark contrast to the grime and clamor below. Nearby, a notice board displays freshly posted taxes, strict curfew rules, and a warning about a patrol that has gone missing somewhere beyond the gate. Among the crowd, a figure in threadbare clothes watches with unnerving stillness, their gaze drifting more toward the packs and faces than the gate line itself. Near the rain barrel, a tavern runner calls out animatedly, offering hot stew for coin alongside whispered rumors, providing an undercurrent of restless chatter to the scene.

The still figure's boots are worn and muddy, fraying at the edges, suggesting long travel without respite. Their hands, visible beneath threadbare sleeves, are rough but steady, indicating a hard life. Near the rain barrel, the mud bears faint impressions of several boot patterns—some recent, others older—interrupted by the scattered remains of a broken wooden crate and a discarded scrap of cloth fluttering in the moist breeze.

The figure's boots are worn and caked with dried mud, matching the threadbare condition of their clothing. Their hands are clasped tightly, revealing cracked knuckles but no obvious injuries or adornments. Scanning the muddy ground near the rain barrel, you notice shallow, indistinct footprints mingled with the usual crowd traffic, but no clear tracks or discarded items stand out in the rain-soaked earth.

You study the notice board carefully. The missing-patrol warning is dated a few days ago, its paper weathered but still sealed with an official stamp matching the city guard’s mark. The handwriting is brisk and authoritative, similar to the tax and curfew notices posted alongside it. The warning was clearly posted after those notices, suggesting urgency in response to the patrol’s absence. Nearby, the gate serjeant’s wary eyes flicker between the crowd and the roster board, a silent reminder of the tension simmering here.

"The patrol left shortly after the Ash Compact census choke deepened," the gate serjeant replies, glancing toward the mud-choked paths leading east. "Their usual route has been altered to skirt the eastern caravan bottleneck, which has grown worse in recent days. As for signs, no clear word has come back — no flags or messages recovered — and their whereabouts remain uncertain." They pause, their gaze drifting to the restless mass pressing the gate. "You'll want to talk to the guard captain inside; they might have updates on any patrol sightings or recovered signals since then."

The roster board lists several patrol members assigned to the missing group, along with their departure time: just after dawn four days ago. Their assigned route is noted to have shifted recently—skirting the northwest mud track past the storage crates—due to increased delays from the Ash Compact census choke. Annotations on the board include a handwritten warning about their delayed return, matching the official notice's dates and handwriting style. There are no updates or recovered signals noted here; for those, you'll want to consult the guard captain inside who may have more recent information.

Following the edge of the northwest mud track, you reach the cluster of storage crates. The ground here is churned with many footprints and ruts from wagons, but you notice no obvious bootprints or guard insignia that stand out against the recent, mixed traffic. The crates themselves appear weathered and partially covered in mud, with no broken gear or discarded items in immediate view that would suggest any recent disturbance aside from the usual bustle.

You carefully circle the storage crates on the muddy northwest track, paying close attention to their sheltered sides, gaps, and bases where the rain has pooled and traffic has pressed mud into every crevice. Despite your thorough inspection, you find no fresh scratches, no cloth snags caught on nails or splinters, and no concealed marks or impressions that survive recent rain and hustle. The older impressions here show the usual signs of wear—wagon ruts and many footsteps—but nothing that sets itself apart as a clue or signature.

You carefully circle the cluster of storage crates, focusing on their sheltered sides, gaps, and muddy bases. Despite the moisture and trampling of recent rain and foot traffic, you find no distinctive scratches, cloth snags, or concealed marks that stand out from the usual wear and tear. Any older impressions have been largely obscured by the steady rain and constant movement around the area.

You return to the gate serjeant, who acknowledges your approach with a curt nod. "The crate route has indeed yielded nothing, as you say," they report, eyes flicking to the roster board. "The guard captain is just inside the gatehouse; they’ve been reviewing reports and might provide fresh insight on sightings or signals since the patrol was marked missing. You’ll find them near the muster table, coordinating the shift and cross-referencing the timeline." The serjeant gestures towards the gatehouse entrance, where the guard captain is unmistakably busy organizing papers and barking quiet orders.

You return to the gate serjeant and inform them that your search around the crates turned up no trace spared by the rain. The serjeant nods, their gaze flicking toward the guarded entry beyond the muddy queue. "The guard captain is inside the gatehouse," they say curtly. "You’ll find them there, overseeing the watch. They might have updates on any patrol sightings or signals since the notice went up."

You stand amid the pressed crowd at Cinderwatch Gate, aware that several factors delay direct access to the guard captain. The captain is not immediately accessible—restricted entry from gate controls plus the busy milling of onlookers and officials at the gate all contribute to this barrier. If you cannot speak with the captain now, the last person known to bring news from the northwest route was a member of the guard patrol sent out four days ago. Further details may be obtained by speaking directly with the gate serjeant or guards managing the crowd and roster nearby.

The guard tending the roster glances over the notice board and replies, "The last news came from a member of the guard patrol sent northwest four days ago with the missing group. They reported signs of trouble along the route, but I didn't see the patrol member return myself—some came back through other gates, and it's unclear if the one who brought the news passed through here." He gestures toward the gate serjeant, suggesting you might get clearer details by speaking with them directly.

"I'm afraid I cannot confirm either account precisely," the gate serjeant replies, his gaze flicking briefly to the notice board where only a warning about the missing patrol is posted. "No formal report has reached us yet, at least nothing recorded on official rosters beyond this caution. If someone claims a patrol member reported trouble, they must have done so outside standard channels, or the message hasn't arrived here. Your best course is to speak directly with the guard captain when possible—he keeps the official accounts and may have more concrete information."

"From what I've gathered," the gate serjeant says, "no direct word has come back to this gate about the patrol since their departure. The guard tending the roster references a report from a patrol member sent northwest four days ago, noting signs of trouble, but I have no official confirmation beyond that. That report is recorded on the notice board here, though details are scant, and no further updates have been logged."
